message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-11-06 05:10 IST to 2026-11-07 05:10 IST

Six newly published vulnerabilities were verified as relevant to the monitored Node.js product through `undici`, the official HTTP client bundled with Node.js. One is High severity and five are Medium. No other fresh, credible match survived the time, product, and source checks.

### CVE-2026-116592: undici cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure

- **Affected product or component:** Node.js / undici 7.30.1 and 8.12.2 through 8.12.3
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 7.4
- **Description:** A redirect that passes through an untrusted origin and returns to a trusted origin can cause a shared cache to store poisoned content or expose a user's private response to another caller.
- **Why it is relevant:** undici is an official Node.js component and Node.js is in the monitored inventory. Exposure depends on the bundled or installed undici version and use of the redirect and shared-cache interceptors.
- **Source:** [GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32)

### CVE-2026-116630: undici cross-origin redirect revalidation disclosure

- **Affected product or component:** Node.js / undici 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3
- **Severity:** Medium, CVSS 5.9
- **Description:** A cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation can let a response from one origin validate cached authenticated content, which may then be served to an unauthenticated caller.
- **Why it is relevant:** This affects the official HTTP client bundled with Node.js when redirect and shared-cache interceptors are composed.
- **Source:** [GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954)

### CVE-2026-120415: undici credential disclosure on redirected requests

- **Affected product or component:** Node.js / undici 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3
- **Severity:** Medium, CVSS 5.9
- **Description:** When headers are provided as name/value tuples, sensitive headers can survive a cross-origin redirect and be sent to the redirect destination.
- **Why it is relevant:** This is an official Node.js HTTP-client component; affected applications must use the vulnerable header representation and interceptor composition.
- **Source:** [GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f)

### CVE-2026-120423: undici Subresource Integrity bypass

- **Affected product or component:** Node.js / undici 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3
- **Severity:** Medium, CVSS 5.9
- **Description:** Whitespace handling in integrity metadata can cause a valid digest to be skipped, allowing modified response content to pass Subresource Integrity checks.
- **Why it is relevant:** Node.js applications using undici `fetch` with affected SRI metadata parsing may accept content that does not match the pinned digest.
- **Source:** [GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc)

### CVE-2026-120222: undici denial of service during cached-response replay

- **Affected product or component:** Node.js / undici 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3
- **Severity:** Medium, CVSS 5.9
- **Description:** An exception raised while replaying a cached response can escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled rejection and terminate the Node.js process.
- **Why it is relevant:** The flaw is in Node.js's official HTTP client and is reachable when the cache interceptor is composed with a response handler that can throw.
- **Source:** [GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2)

### CVE-2026-120474: undici same-origin redirect cache disclosure

- **Affected product or component:** Node.js / undici 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3
- **Severity:** Medium, CVSS 6.5
- **Description:** A private authenticated response reached through a same-origin redirect can be cached under a key that omits credentials and later served to another user.
- **Why it is relevant:** This affects the official Node.js HTTP client when redirects and a shared response cache are used together.
- **Source:** [GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg)

### MongoDB ecosystem sweep

The dedicated sweep covered MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and libraries, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, and official integrations. No fresh, credible MongoDB finding was verified inside the 24-hour window. The newest item on the [official MongoDB alerts page](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts) was dated 2026-10-28 and was excluded as stale.

**Closing:** Prompt review is recommended for Node.js deployments that bundle or install affected undici versions, especially applications using redirect and shared-cache interceptors. No immediate MongoDB action is indicated from this scan.
